hero.title: 40 products. One reactive core.
hero.lede: Forms, charts, routing, auth, i18n, a native compiler and the tools that check all of it, built together on the same signals and released as one version. Use one in the app you have, or build the whole thing on them.

groupingNote: Follows products.html with two fixes: HTTP moves from Foundations to Data and state (it is the transport under Query, and the mega menu already files it there), and Content moves from Visual and content to Build apps (it is Zero's content layer and cannot run without Zero). RX stays in Data and state, as on products.html.

groups.title: Build apps
groups.text: The framework, the native compiler and the pieces every app starts from.

groups.title: Foundations
groups.text: Small, sharp packages you reach for on day one.

groups.title: Data and state
groups.text: Forms, server data, shared state and the rules around them. All signals.

groups.title: Visual and content
groups.text: Charts, grids, editors and diagrams that stay fast when the data gets big.

groups.title: Developer tools
groups.text: The tools that check your code, your components, your API and your monorepo.

products.name: Native
products.pitch: Compile one `.tsx` into a real SwiftUI app and a real Jetpack Compose app, tested on an iOS Simulator and an Android emulator in CI. Experimental, and labelled that way.

products.name: Zero
products.pitch: Every route picks its own rendering: SSG, SSR, ISR or SPA, plus islands, server actions and adapters for Node, Bun, Deno, Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare and static hosts.

proof.label: faster server rendering than React 19 at 1,000 rows (compiled SSR, 109.9 vs 714.4 µs)
proof.condition: one run, overnight pass, M3 Max, synthetic, author-run

products.name: Content
products.pitch: Markdown and MDX compiled to real Pyreon JSX at build time, with Astro-style typed collections checked by your own Zod, Valibot or ArkType schema.

products.name: Primitives
products.pitch: Components from `<Stack>` and `<Field>` to `<Toggle>` and `<Modal>` (22 in the next release) that render DOM on the web and real SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose views on phones (native: experimental).

products.name: Design System
products.pitch: Eleven packages: `styled()` CSS-in-JS, components styled by state × size × variant × dark mode, a responsive grid and transitions, all cached and SSR-safe.

proof.label: timed operations where the styler beat both Emotion and goober (cold insert, warm dedup, dynamic resolve, SSR collect)

products.name: Auth
products.pitch: OIDC sign-in on the web, and on iOS and Android (experimental), from one call, with S256 PKCE, `state`, `nonce` and the issuer check on by default, plus signed sessions, TOTP and passkeys.

products.name: Reactivity
products.pitch: `signal`, `computed`, `effect`, `batch`: the core every Pyreon package runs on, and it works on its own.

proof.label: faster effect propagation than Preact Signals

products.name: Router
products.pitch: Params typed from the path string (`/user/:id` gives `{ id: string }`), with loaders, guards, middleware, typed search params and View Transitions.

products.name: Hooks
products.pitch: 65 signal-based hooks, 45 of them also on iOS and Android (experimental), from `useClickOutside` and `useMediaQuery` to `useCamera` and `useBiometrics`.

products.name: Motion
products.pitch: Enter, leave and height collapse from one `kinetic(tag)` factory, 122 presets, and SSR output crawlers can read.

products.name: Accessibility
products.pitch: `announce('Saved')` reaches screen readers with no provider and no setup; `<LiveRegion>`, `<VisuallyHidden>` and SSR-safe ids cover the rest.

products.name: Drag and Drop
products.pitch: Drag and drop on Atlassian's pragmatic-drag-and-drop engine: sortable lists with keyboard reordering, file drop, and every drag state as a signal.

products.name: Toast
products.pitch: `toast('Saved')` from anywhere, no provider; `toast.promise()` for async work, and the timer pauses on hover, on focus and in a hidden tab.

proof.label: faster headless toast operations than react-hot-toast

products.name: Forms
products.pitch: Every field is its own signal, so typing in one field never touches the other eleven. Pass a Zod, Valibot or ArkType schema raw, no adapter.

proof.label: faster mount than React Hook Form (12 fields, 210 vs 640 µs); fastest of 7 libraries on all 4 timed ops
proof.condition: one run, overnight pass, real Chromium

products.name: Validation
products.pitch: A chainable validator (`s.string().email()`) that speaks Standard Schema, with field metadata, reactive parse and translated errors built in.

proof.label: cells won against zod, valibot and arktype on a multi-schema workload

products.name: Query
products.pitch: TanStack Query on signals: `data`, `error` and `isFetching` are separate signals, and WebSocket and SSE hooks share the same cache.

proof.label: derivations per data change, against react-query on the same TanStack core
proof.condition: happy-dom count, one run, overnight pass

products.name: HTTP
products.pitch: The request layer under Query: onion middleware, typed errors, cancellation and optional schema validation, on a zero-dependency core.

products.name: Store
products.pitch: Global state is a setup function that returns signals and functions. Actions, patches, subscriptions and per-request SSR isolation come with it.

products.name: State Tree
products.pitch: MobX-State-Tree-style models on signals: typed snapshots, JSON-patch record and replay, middleware, and per-request isolation on the server.

proof.label: faster actions than MobX-State-Tree

products.name: State Machines
products.pitch: A state machine that is a signal: it holds only the states you list and moves only by named events, with typed guards.

proof.label: faster `send` than XState

products.name: Storage
products.pitch: Signals that persist: localStorage synced across tabs, sessionStorage, cookies the server can read, and IndexedDB, all behind one API.

proof.label: faster writes than Jotai atomWithStorage and Zustand persist (10.1–29.7×)

products.name: Sync
products.pitch: Local-first sync where a synced value is a normal signal, so a remote edit is one DOM update. Yjs underneath, IndexedDB offline, a WebSocket relay with per-room auth.

products.name: Feature
products.pitch: Hand `defineFeature` a schema and an API path. Get list, detail, search, create, update and delete, plus the form, the table and the store.

products.name: Permissions
products.pitch: `can('posts.edit')` is a reactive check, so the UI follows when roles change. RBAC, ABAC, feature flags and plan tiers, with `posts.*` wildcards.

proof.label: faster than CASL on a fair resolver race

products.name: URL State
products.pitch: `useUrlState('page', 1)` is a signal synced to the query string, with type coercion and `replaceState`, so filters survive a refresh and a pasted link.

proof.label: faster array parsing than nuqs

products.name: i18n
products.pitch: Translations with Intl-correct plurals, number, date and relative-time formatting, and namespaces that load when a page needs them.

proof.label: faster `t()` than i18next

products.name: RX
products.pitch: 43 functions (`filter`, `sortBy`, `groupBy`, `pipe`, `debounce`…) that take signals and return signals.

proof.label: a `pipe()` of N stages runs as one reactive node (exact count)
proof.condition: final pass, node count, not a timing

products.name: Charts
products.pitch: Charts written as JSX marks (`<Line>`, `<Bar>`, `<Area>`) on Pyreon's own engine, with an accessible data table built in and the same source on iOS and Android (experimental).

proof.label: faster than ECharts 6 mounting a 100,000-point line chart (4.36 vs 37.95 ms)
proof.condition: one run, final pass, real Chromium

products.name: Table
products.pitch: TanStack Table's headless core with signal-driven state and reactive options, rendered by Pyreon's fine-grained DOM.

proof.label: faster than @tanstack/react-table (memoized rows) replacing 1,000 rows
proof.condition: two runs, final pass, real Chromium

products.name: Virtual
products.pitch: TanStack Virtual for element or window scrolling: a 10,000-row list with only the visible rows in the DOM.

proof.label: ops won against @tanstack/react-virtual (mount, scroll, jump, unmount)
proof.condition: one run, final pass, real Chromium

products.name: Editors
products.pitch: Rich text on TipTap and code on CodeMirror 6, where the document is a signal. Lazy-loaded languages, a minimap and a diff editor included.

products.name: Flow
products.pitch: Node editors where each node mounts once and a drag touches one node, with auto-layout from its own engine: no dagre, no elkjs.

proof.label: operations won against React Flow 12 (500 nodes): mount, drag, select, add, pan and zoom, unmount
proof.condition: one run, real Chromium, synthetic, author-run
proof.source: 00-brief/BENCHMARKS-2026-11-05.md §2 flow vs React Flow 12: wins all six ops, 1.17–210×, one run. Headline uses 6/6, not 210×: the record says the drag/pan ratios are mostly React Flow re-rendering node wrappers

products.name: Documents
products.pitch: One template, 20 output formats: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, email, Markdown, Slack, Teams, Notion and more. Heavy renderers load only when used.

products.name: Hotkeys
products.pitch: Scoped keyboard shortcuts with modifier keys and conflict detection, unregistered when their component unmounts.

proof.label: faster dispatch than tinykeys, hotkeys-js and mousetrap

products.name: Tooling
products.pitch: `pyreon doctor` runs up to ten gates over your app and scores it 0–100 with the fixes inline, next to 133 lint rules, `pyreon check`, a test kit and devtools for the reactive graph.

products.name: AI and MCP
products.pitch: An MCP server with 24 tools: your assistant looks up the real API, validates its code against Pyreon's misuse detectors and explains reactivity. No network calls.

products.name: Atlas
products.pitch: A component catalog derived from your components and types: controls from props, scenarios from variants, and a six-check verdict per scenario (a11y, interaction, leak, SSR parity, reactivity, snapshot).

products.name: Lathe
products.pitch: OpenAPI in, typed Pyreon client out: schemas, endpoints, query hooks, mocks and docs. `lathe check` fails CI when the generated code drifts from the spec.

products.name: Loom
products.pitch: Your workspace's dependency graph as data: version drift, runtime cycles, phantom deps and blast radius, with a non-zero exit for CI.

proof.label: to scan the Pyreon monorepo, warm (98.3% of it import scanning)
proof.condition: one run, overnight pass, Pyreon-only figure

products.name: Migrate
products.pitch: Compat layers for React, Preact, Vue, Solid and Svelte with near-full public-API parity: change the imports, keep shipping, port screens when it pays.

underneath.text: Underneath sit the compiler, both runtimes, the server, head management and the rest of the 77 published packages. Each one is covered on the product page that uses it.

proofFooter: Proof numbers: benchmark record of 5 Nov 2026, Apple M3 Max, synthetic and author-run. Every loss is published too.

end.title: Start with one. The other 39 will wait.
end.text: Scaffold a Zero app with forms, query and the store wired in, or add a single package to the app you already have.

tertiary.label: Don't trust us. Run the benchmarks.
